Quick pass (coordinator, read only, no build) on head `2e7f78856`: the PR is a sub-PR of `side/path-kernel` and merges cleanly with it (`25f3838db`). It is sub-PR 2 of 2 for #4176: the medial line, the trace and the helix guide planners. The author's gate is green on this head: `cargo check --tests` for pathkernel, geometry and motion; the quick gate, which became a full batch run because `camcraft-geometry` changes (1223 steps, 0 failed, clippy and the three example catalog suites included); and the light lane (7 steps). The writer record on #4176 is released. The body starts with `Side branch: side/path-kernel` and has `Refs #4176`. The PR is flagged ready. It waits for the independent review.

Notes for the reviewer:
- The trial merge and the gate base are `origin/side/path-kernel`.
- The safety floor applies: the guide curves decide where the tool cuts. No old planner calls the new code; with the default switch the output is identical.
- The PR adds a medial axis to `camcraft-geometry` (`geo2d/medial.rs`, `geo2d/delaunay.rs`, `geo2d/side_offset.rs`). It is new geometry code from published literature, not a port of the old spine. Check the provenance, and that degenerate input gives a refusal and never a crash or a hang.
- The PR also changes `crates/pathkernel/src/region.rs` and adds `region_chain.rs` (the region of a trace along a chain). The follow-up #4236 says that the later stages do not accept that region yet.
- The differences from the recorded old guides are named in the header of `pass_start_levels/kernel_guides.rs` and in the decision file.
- PR #4234 (order and link) is open at the same time, with a review fix in work. The two PRs add lines to the same module lists and to `camcraft-geometry`. The PR that merges second takes a merge of the side branch.

Label: needs-rework - review found one item before merge (the trace chain region's downstream refusal is explicit but unpinned; see the review comment). The other state labels were removed (none were on this PR).

Review fix for head 2e7f78856: commit ebc966350 closes the one finding (the downstream refusal of the trace chain region is not pinned).

The class rule: one table test, `guide_trace::each_later_stage_refuses_the_chain_region_of_a_trace_by_name`, gives the chain region of a trace to each later stage on this branch that reads the region. Each stage must refuse it by its named reason. A panic or an accepted plan makes the test fail.

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| `EntryStage::entry` | refused, `entry::NOT_PLANAR` |
| `EntryStage::exit` | refused, `entry::NOT_PLANAR` |
| law kit `planar` | refused, `kit::NOT_PLANAR` |
| law kit `run` | refused, `kit::NOT_PLANAR` |

The order, load and link stages have no planner on this branch (traits only). The test comment names #4236, which makes these stages accept the region. No stage logic changed: no stage panicked or accepted the region.

Checks on head ebc966350:
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The quick plan against `origin/side/path-kernel` is the full batch again (1223 steps), because the whole PR changes geometry. The fix changes only one test file. So I ran the pathkernel suites, the geometry suites and clippy by name: 41 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The full batch ran green on 2e7f78856 (1223 steps).

The new head waits for a fresh review.

- `crates/pathkernel/src/guide.rs`: K4 changed `Curve::same_cut` to `turn_of`, which returns `Option<bool>`. This branch added the lead check of a helix. The two changes do not exclude each other: `turn_of` keeps the lead check and returns `None` when the leads differ.

Other changes in the merge commit:

Label: needs-rework - the review found one item before merge (the order stage refuses a helix guide set with the misleading HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD reason: the K4 reversed() rebuilds any curve via Curve::new, which refuses the helix family; see the review comment). No merge-ready (needs the fix); no conflicts (the PR merges cleanly with side/path-kernel at 7f70d8b1a and at the current base df9ec30b6).

Review fix: commit 6aa630fee closes the requested change of the review at 33c116cfa (the order stage refused a helix guide set with `HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD`).

Class of the finding: a later stage made a curve again with a constructor that is not the constructor of the curve's family. The fix applies one rule to the class:
- A later stage that restarts, reverses or replaces a curve makes it again through the constructor of its family (`Curve::with_points`: `Curve::helix` with the same circle and lead, else `Curve::new` with the same circle).
- If the stage cannot do that, it refuses by a reason of its own stage.

What each stage does with a helix:
- Order: a helix always runs down its lead. A reversal in the plane also turns it up its lead, so the stage reverses it only when the guide set holds it upward. The hand sets the side of the material. When the asked direction is the other one, the stage keeps the helix down its lead and adds the order note `HELIX_HAND_SETS_DIRECTION`. A failed rebuild is the order reason `NOT_REVERSIBLE`.
- Load: constant engagement inserts no pass before a curve that is not a ring (`NOT_A_RING`). Trochoidal loops do not change a curve with a lead, an exact circle or a changing depth (`SHAPE_KEPT`). A rebuilt set that is refused is `SET_NOT_KEPT`.
- Link and entry: they read the curve and make no new curve.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix.md`.

What the table covers (`later_stages::each_guide_family_keeps_its_data_or_is_refused_by_the_stage_in_each_later_stage`):
- Rows: rings of a pocket, exact circle rings of a hole, rows, the medial line of a slot, the trace of an open chain, the right-hand helix of the review (red before the fix), and a left-hand helix of four turns.
- Columns: `OrderStage` with each start side and each direction, `LoadStage` with none, constant engagement on the rings, constant engagement on the stock and trochoidal, `LinkStage`, and the entry and exit of `EntryStage`.
- Each cell runs under `catch_unwind`. A result must keep the circle, the lead and the marks (the order output is a permutation, law 3), and a helix must run down its lead. A refusal must come from the stage of the cell and must not carry a constructor's reason.
- A second test pins the review's exact case and the note for each hand and direction.
- The trace chain-region table has three new `LoadStage` rows (`LOAD_NOT_PLANAR`).
- With the old reversal, the two new tests are red with `HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD` from the Guide stage. With the fix, they are green.
